newsitem.title: UK: CBI's Barker sees no medium term UK wage pressures.
newsitem.headline: CBI's Barker sees no medium term UK wage pressures.

text.p: British wages are unlikely to be pushed higher in the medium-term despite a skills gap in some industries, Kate Barker, chief economic adviser at the Confederation of British Industry said on Monday.
"Skill shortages are likely to be in specific pockets," Barker, who is also one of Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's independent advisers, said.
Those shortages could be dealt with by retraining, she said, and were not likely to "drive up wages over the medium-term."

Barker was commenting on the CBI/Coopers & Lybrand survey on Britain's financial services, which showed an increase in the number of people employed in the sector for the first time since September 1995.
Official figures showed annualised average earnings growth was running at five percent in January. Late last year, the Office for National Statistics had put wages growth at just four percent.
